explanation.text: Before any purchase, holdings labelled Energy are already between 1.4% and 16.8% of the portfolio (through XIU.TO), above the confirmed tolerance of 0.0%. The purchase itself adds 0.3% (Exxon Mobil through SPY).

Holdings labelled Energy are between 1.7% and 17.1% of the portfolio after the purchase: 1.4% through XIU.TO (Enbridge, Canadian Natural Resources), 0.3% through SPY (Exxon Mobil), and up to 15.4% that cannot be ruled out because ESGV has no holdings file and XIU.TO is 98% covered. The confirmed tolerance is 0.0%: the rule fails.

No held company has a matching record in the controversy registry, and the registry covers none of the held companies. Absence from the registry means not assessed, so this rule is UNKNOWN, not passed.

No purchase of SPY can make every confirmed rule pass with cash funding: the Energy-label exclusion is already breached by the starting portfolio (1.4% through XIU.TO), and buying does not reduce it. Bringing it to 0 would require selling, which this funding path does not support.
The Energy label is the sector reported in each fund's holdings file. It is not a list of oil producers and it says nothing about controversies.
This is a simulation on a fictional portfolio. It is not advice, and no trade is made.
